body: Goemon's Great Adventure is Konami's Nintendo 64 platformer about recovering a stolen resurrection machine and stopping the revived ruler of the underworld. Goemon, Ebisumaru, Sasuke and Yae travel through five worlds filled with monsters, towns and anachronistic machinery. The action follows a side-scrolling path through three-dimensional scenery, allowing the route to bend through the environment while remaining clearly defined. Two players can travel together, giving the familiar comic cast another way to share the work of crossing an obstacle or confronting an enemy.

An overworld connects stages, settlements and dungeons. Completing levels and helping people in town earns the entry passes needed to reach later destinations. Each character's abilities provide another approach to the platforming, while portals and towns allow a change of companion. The route therefore includes reasons to pause, speak to somebody and attempt a task beyond merely reaching the next stage's exit. Different paths and optional discoveries give the surrounding world more activity than a simple line of levels would provide.

Cooperative players share the visible space, requiring them to make progress together rather than run independently into different parts of the level. That limitation makes agreement about the next jump or enemy useful in itself. Musical themes, Japanese folklore and giant robot encounters preserve the series' exuberant character. Released overseas in 1999, and called Mystical Ninja 2 Starring Goemon in Europe, the game uses the newer console's depth to stage an adventure whose movement remains closely related to the series' earlier side-scrolling outings.
